q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path lying on a plane that is in what orientation to the axis?
e: All particles move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis.

q: What is the relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $\theta$ (measured in radians)?
e: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $\theta$, measured in radian, is $s = r\theta$.

q: What is the relation between the magnitude of linear velocity $v$ and angular velocity $\omega$ of a particle in rotational motion?
e: The relation between the magnitude of the linear velocity $v$ and the angular velocity $\omega$ is $v = r\omega$.

q: Which property of a rotational object is the same for all the particles comprising the object?
e: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ of a rotational object is the same for all the particles comprising the object.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, what is another name for linear velocity in rotational motion?
e: Because its direction is tangent to the path, linear velocity is also called tangential velocity.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity of a rotating object changes, what type of acceleration does the object experience?
e: A change in the magnitude of angular velocity means the magnitude of linear velocity changes, resulting in tangential acceleration.

q: What is the direction of tangential acceleration?
a: Always towards the centre of the circular path
Always perpendicular to the circular path
Always tangent to the circular path
Always along the axis of rotation
e: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path.

q: What is the equation relating tangential acceleration $a_T$ to angular acceleration $\alpha$?
e: The tangential acceleration $a_T$ relates to angular acceleration $\alpha$ by the equation $a_T = r\alpha$.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of what?
a: How fast the angular displacement changes
How fast the centripetal acceleration changes
How fast the tangential velocity changes
How fast the angular velocity changes
e: The textbook explicitly states that tangential acceleration is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes.

q: What is the direction of the angular velocity vector?
a: Tangent to the plane of rotation
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation, along the axis of rotation
Towards the centre of the circular path
Parallel to the linear velocity vector
e: The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation, and along the axis of rotation.

q: Which rule is usually used to specify the direction of angular velocity?
e: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the right-hand rule.

q: According to the right-hand rule, which part of the hand points in the direction of the angular velocity vector?
e: When wrapping the right hand around the axis, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, in what direction does the angular acceleration vector point?
a: In the same direction as the angular velocity
In the opposite direction to the angular velocity
e: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, in what direction does the angular acceleration vector point?
a: In the same direction as the angular velocity
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation
e: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite to the angular velocity.
